questions.text: For a given binary sequence (e.g. 100000000001101 or 110011000001), draw the resulting waveforms for: Unipolar RZ, Polar NRZ, Bipolar AMI, Manchester, and HDB3 / B8ZS scrambling line codes. Discuss DC component, clock recovery, and bandwidth requirements.

What is the aim of source coding? For a given message string with character frequencies, construct the Huffman code tree, generate binary codewords, and calculate source entropy $H(X)$, average codeword length $L$, coding efficiency $\eta = \frac{H(X)}{L}$, and redundancy.

A $(6, 3)$ linear block code has a specified parity check matrix $H$. (a) Determine the generator matrix $G$, (b) Generate the valid codeword for message vector $m = [1, 1, 0]$, (c) Compute the syndrome vector $S = r H^T$ for a received word $r$ and demonstrate single-bit error detection and correction.
Draw and explain the constellation diagram of 16-QAM and 32-QAM. Compare QAM with QPSK and Minimum Shift Keying (MSK) in terms of bandwidth efficiency, bit error rate, and constant envelope property.

Derive the impulse response $h(t) = s(T-t)$ and maximum output signal-to-noise ratio ($SNR = \frac{2E}{N_0}$) of a Matched Filter receiver operating in an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel.

State the Shannon-Hartley Channel Capacity Theorem: $C = B \log_2\left(1 + \frac{S}{N}\right)$. Discuss the trade-off between bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio, and prove the Shannon capacity limit: $\frac{E_b}{N_0} \ge \ln 2 = -1.59\text{ dB}$ as channel bandwidth approaches infinity.

Derive the mathematical expression for double-tone Amplitude Modulation (AM). Calculate the percentage of total transmitted power saved in DSB-SC and SSB-SC as compared to standard AM with modulation index $\mu = 1$.

Explain Armstrong's indirect method for generating Wideband Frequency Modulation (WBFM) from Narrowband FM using frequency multipliers and mixers. Why are Pre-emphasis and De-emphasis filtering circuits used in FM broadcast?

Why is non-uniform quantization required in telephony? Explain $\mu$-law and A-law logarithmic companding curves. Prove that for a standard voice channel ($300\text{ Hz} - 3.4\text{ kHz}$), 8-bit PCM sampled at $8\text{ kHz}$ yields a bit rate of $64\text{ kbps}$.

Compare Pulse Code Modulation (PCM), Differential Pulse Code Modulation (DPCM), and Delta Modulation (DM). Explain slope overload distortion and granular noise in Delta Modulation and how Adaptive Delta Modulation (ADM) solves them.

Compare Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) with Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM). Compare T1 ($1.544\text{ Mbps}$, 24 channels) and E1 ($2.048\text{ Mbps}$, 32 channels) digital PCM transmission hierarchies with frame structures.

Explain the operation of a Superheterodyne Receiver with a block diagram. Explain RF amplifier, mixer, Intermediate Frequency (IF), Automatic Gain Control (AGC), and Image Frequency Rejection Ratio (IFRR).

For a rate-1/2 convolutional encoder with given generator polynomials, draw the State Diagram, Tree Diagram, and Trellis Diagram. Explain how the Viterbi decoding algorithm performs maximum-likelihood path decoding.

What is the Hilbert Transform? State its essential properties. Explain how the Hilbert transform is used to generate Single Sideband Suppressed Carrier (SSB-SC) modulated signals using the phase-shift method.

Define Noise Figure ($F$), Equivalent Noise Temperature ($T_e$), and Noise Factor in cascaded stages (Friis formula for noise). Derive the Figure of Merit $(\gamma = \frac{SNR_o}{SNR_c})$ for SSB, DSB-SC, and AM receivers.
Define Auto-correlation and Cross-correlation for energy and power signals. State and prove the Wiener-Khinchin theorem relating the autocorrelation function and the Power Spectral Density (PSD).

Sketch and describe the functional block diagram of a digital communication system operating in duplex mode. Contrast it with an analog communication system and discuss channel impairments (attenuation, distortion, noise, interference).
questions.solutionOutline: Blocks: Information source, Source Encoder, Channel Encoder, Digital Modulator, Transmission Channel, Digital Demodulator, Channel Decoder, Source Decoder, Transducer. Digital advantages: high noise immunity, regenerative repeaters, cryptographic security, uniform multiplexing of diverse media types.

questions.text: Derive the mathematical expression for Standard Amplitude Modulated (DSB-FC) wave. Calculate modulation index $\mu$, total transmitted power $P_t = P_c(1 + \frac{\mu^2}{2})$, and modulation efficiency $\eta$. Why does standard AM waste over $66.7\%$ of transmitted power in the carrier?
questions.solutionOutline: s(t) = A_c [1 + mu m_n(t)] cos(2 pi f_c t). Total power P_t = P_c + P_USB + P_LSB = P_c(1 + mu^2/2). Sideband power ratio eta = mu^2 / (2 + mu^2). For 100% modulation (mu = 1), sidebands contain only 1/3 (33.3%) of power, while 2/3 (66.7%) is wasted in redundant carrier. Solved by DSB-SC and SSB-SC.

questions.text: Derive the time-domain equation and frequency spectrum for Frequency Modulated (FM) signal with single-tone sinusoidal modulation. Explain Carson's Rule for FM bandwidth $B_T = 2(\Delta f + f_m)$ and frequency demodulation using Phase Locked Loop (PLL).
questions.solutionOutline: Instantaneous frequency f_i(t) = f_c + k_f m(t). s_FM(t) = A_c cos(2 pi f_c t + beta sin(2 pi f_m t)), expanding into Bessel series sum J_n(beta) cos(2 pi (f_c + n f_m) t). Carson Rule accounts for sidebands carrying 98% of power: B_T = 2(Delta f + f_m) = 2 f_m (1 + beta). PLL tracks input frequency through phase detector, loop filter, and VCO.

questions.text: Explain Pulse Code Modulation (PCM). Detail the processes of Sampling, Uniform vs Non-uniform Quantization, and Encoding. Derive the signal-to-quantization noise ratio formula $(S/N_q) = 1.8 + 6n \text{ dB}$ for an $n$-bit quantizer. Compare $\mu$-law and A-law companding.
questions.solutionOutline: PCM converts analog to digital sequence. Quantization error e in [-Delta/2, Delta/2] has variance sigma_e^2 = Delta^2/12. With step size Delta = 2V_max / 2^n, SNR_q = 3 * 2^(2n) * (P / V_max^2), giving SNR_dB = 1.76 + 6.02 n dB. Companding applies non-linear compression before uniform quantization to maintain uniform SNR for weak speech signals (mu-law: North America/Japan; A-law: Europe/Nepal).

questions.text: State the Nyquist Criterion for Zero Intersymbol Interference (ISI). Derive the condition on transfer function $H(f)$ for distortionless baseband pulse transmission. Explain the Raised Cosine roll-off filter and the concept of excess bandwidth factor ($\alpha$).
questions.solutionOutline: Nyquist criterion states sum_{k} H(f - k R_b) = T_b = constant. Minimum theoretical bandwidth B_min = R_b/2 for ideal brick-wall sinc pulses. Raised Cosine filter introduces practical gradual transition band with roll-off factor alpha in [0, 1]. Total bandwidth B = (1 + alpha) R_b / 2. Higher alpha reduces ISI sensitivity and timing jitter at expense of bandwidth.

questions.text: Explain Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) and Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK). Draw transmitter and receiver block diagrams, signal constellations, and derive the probability of bit error $P_b = Q\left(\sqrt{\frac{2E_b}{N_0}}\right)$ for coherent BPSK.
questions.solutionOutline: BPSK shifts carrier phase by 180 degrees: s_1(t) = sqrt(2 E_b / T_b) cos(2 pi f_c t), s_2(t) = -s_1(t). Decision distance d_12 = 2 sqrt(E_b). P_b = Q(d_12 / 2 sigma) = Q(sqrt(2 E_b / N_0)). QPSK splits bit stream into In-phase (I) and Quadrature (Q) streams with 4 constellation points separated by 90 degrees, achieving double bandwidth efficiency (2 bits/s/Hz) with identical bit error rate.

questions.text: State the Shannon-Hartley Channel Capacity Theorem $C = B \log_2\left(1 + \frac{S}{N}\right)$. Prove that as bandwidth $B \to \infty$, the channel capacity approaches the Shannon Limit $C_{\infty} = \frac{S}{N_0 \ln 2} \approx 1.44 \frac{S}{N_0}$ and determine the minimum $E_b/N_0 = -1.59 \text{ dB}$.
questions.solutionOutline: C = B log2(1 + S / (N_0 B)). Let x = S / (N_0 B); as B -> infty, x -> 0. C = (S/N_0) * log2(1 + x)^(1/x) -> (S/N_0) log2(e) = 1.442 S/N_0. Since S = C * E_b, we obtain C <= (C E_b / N_0) / ln 2 => E_b / N_0 >= ln 2 = 0.693 = -1.59 dB, the absolute fundamental limit for error-free digital transmission.

questions.text: Explain Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) codes. Given generator polynomial $G(X) = X^4 + X + 1$ and message bits $M = 1101011011$, compute the transmitted codeword using modulo-2 polynomial division. Show how the receiver detects an error if a bit flips during transmission.
questions.solutionOutline: Append r = degree(G) = 4 zeros to M: M(X)*X^4. Perform modulo-2 polynomial division by G(X). Remainder R(X) is appended to message: Codeword T(X) = M(X)*X^4 + R(X). Receiver divides received vector R_rx(X) by G(X); non-zero remainder (syndrome) signals transmission error.

questions.text: Describe Convolutional Encoding and Viterbi Decoding. For a rate $r = 1/2$ convolutional encoder with generator polynomials $g_1 = (1, 1, 1)$ and $g_2 = (1, 0, 1)$, draw the state transition diagram, tree diagram, and trellis diagram. Trace Viterbi decoding of a received bit stream.
questions.solutionOutline: Convolutional codes have memory: output depends on current bit and previous m shift register stages. Trellis diagram represents states across time intervals. Viterbi algorithm implements maximum likelihood decoding: calculates branch metrics (Hamming distance), accumulates path metrics at each node, and prunes non-survivor paths to find minimum metric path.

questions.text: Explain Spread Spectrum Communication principles. Compare Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) and Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum (FHSS). Define Pseudo-Noise (PN) sequence properties and calculate Processing Gain ($PG = B_{ss}/B$).
questions.solutionOutline: Spread spectrum expands signal transmission bandwidth well beyond minimum necessary information bandwidth using independent pseudo-random code. DSSS multiplies baseband data directly with high chip-rate PN sequence. FHSS shifts carrier frequency rapidly among wide set of hopping channels. Processing Gain PG = B_ss / B_info = T_b / T_c. High PG provides anti-jamming and low probability of intercept.

questions.text: Compare Frequency Division Multiple Access (FDMA), Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA), and Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) in terms of spectrum allocation, synchronization requirements, and the near-far effect.
questions.solutionOutline: FDMA assigns dedicated non-overlapping frequency bands with guard bands. TDMA allocates entire frequency channel in cyclically repeated time slots with guard times (requires precise frame synchronization). CDMA shares same frequency band continuously using orthogonal pseudo-random spreading codes (Walsh/Gold). Near-far problem occurs in CDMA when strong nearby transmitter drowns out distant user; solved by precise closed-loop power control.

questions.text: Define Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN), Equivalent Noise Temperature ($T_e$), and Noise Figure ($F$). Derive Friis' formula for the overall noise factor of a multi-stage cascaded amplifier: $F = F_1 + \frac{F_2 - 1}{G_1} + \frac{F_3 - 1}{G_1 G_2}$.
questions.solutionOutline: AWGN has flat two-sided power spectral density S_N(f) = N_0/2 and Gaussian amplitude distribution. Noise figure F = (SNR_in) / (SNR_out) = 1 + T_e / T_0. Friis formula proves that first stage amplifier noise dominates the cascaded system: high first stage gain G_1 suppresses noise contributions from all succeeding stages.

questions.text: Explain the working of Delta Modulation (DM) system. Describe the causes and waveforms of Slope Overload Distortion and Granular Noise. How does Adaptive Delta Modulation (ADM) overcome these limitations?
questions.solutionOutline: DM transmits 1-bit per sample indicating whether signal increased (+Delta) or decreased (-Delta). Slope overload occurs when slope of input signal exceeds max tracking rate: |dm/dt| > Delta / T_s. Granular noise occurs when signal varies slowly compared to step size Delta. ADM dynamically increases step size during steep slopes and decreases step size during flat signal regions.

questions.text: What is an Eye Pattern (Eye Diagram)? Explain how an eye pattern is generated on an oscilloscope and how it is used to measure ISI, optimum sampling instant, timing jitter, sensitivity to timing error, and noise margin in digital communication systems.
questions.solutionOutline: Display formed by superimposing successive symbol waveforms synchronized to symbol clock rate on an oscilloscope. Eye opening height indicates noise margin against error. Optimum sampling instant is point of maximum eye opening. Eye width indicates time interval over which sampling can occur without error. Slope of eye edge measures sensitivity to timing jitter.
